significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that factual recall follows the ordered relation "shared, language-agnostic retrieval stage" in mid-layer MLPs followed by a "language-specific surfacing stage" in later layers, a form-(iii) claim because it predicts how cross-lingual causal transfer changes with layer rather than merely asserting that a shared representation exists. It establishes both a factual-recall phenomenon and a causal mechanism, fixing where multilingual editing should target; this matters to the MLP-memory account used by Geva et al. (2021) and Meng et al. (2022), because it determines whether one retrieval intervention should propagate across languages or whether knowledge must be edited separately. The claim is determinate, and a negative result would rule out its strong assertion that "the same key-value memory is queried regardless of query language," although it would not by itself select among distributed, partially shared, and language-specific alternatives. After topic substitution, generic shared-versus-specific multilingual processing would not earn this score; the extra weight comes specifically from the predicted retrieval-before-surfacing ordering and its consequence for factual editing.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "layer boundary between shared and specific stages," a "single cross-lingual attribute direction," and the resulting design rule of editing the shared retrieval layer rather than a late language-specific layer. The attribute direction is a forward-looking internal predictor because it is claimed to predict the answer "before language-specific unembedding," while the boundary also supplies an ex-ante choice of intervention site rather than merely explaining an edit after failure. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive prediction—high cross-lingual transfer in mid layers followed by failure when patched too late—still specifies an ordering expected in another multilingual Transformer, though the stated scope is factual associations and explicitly may not extend to reasoning-derived facts; likely downstream users are multilingual model editors and auditors. The topic alone would provide no particular reusable boundary, predictor, or editing rule, so the topic-substitution check preserves an above-median score based on these claim-specific handles.
